about: Metadata for every chapter of the story, in story order. Derived from content/story by npm run library and checked by the gate. Never edited by hand.

chapters.title: Hola, Bogotá
chapters.hook: Rosa's café is closed, there's a letter from Altamira in Tomás's hand, and Don Hernando still hasn't had his morning tinto. For Hernando, that last one is the real emergency.

chapters.title: Un tinto, por favor
chapters.hook: Hernando still has no tinto, and Tomás still hasn't opened Altamira's letter. Tomorrow Vale shows him what a real day in Rosa's café looks like, starting before sunrise.

chapters.title: Las seis
chapters.hook: Just a few days? Tomás has a plan, and he hasn't told Vale.

chapters.title: El señor Ruiz
chapters.hook: Vale heard every word. Tomorrow she has a question for Tomás, and then an offer he really doesn't want.

chapters.title: Treinta días
chapters.hook: Tomás has thirty days. Vale has a plan, Hernando has a plan, and Simón has his eye on everybody's breakfast.

chapters.title: El sábado abrimos
chapters.hook: Saturday, six o'clock. The café opens its doors for the first time since Rosa died. What could possibly go wrong?

chapters.title: Cuarenta libras de mango
chapters.hook: Twelve taxi drivers want a discount, there are still mangoes everywhere, and tomorrow their wives are coming. Nobody has bought a single vegetable.

chapters.title: El señor Mango
chapters.hook: Monday morning: twenty-eight days left, $1.588.000 still to make, and the espresso machine is still dead. Then Vale's phone rings, and it's Medellín.

chapters.title: ¿Es guapo?
chapters.hook: Hernando has brought photos of his grandchildren, and on the shelf there is an album of Rosa's that Tomás has never opened. Tomorrow he opens it.

chapters.title: El álbum de Rosa
chapters.hook: Hernando knows something, and he has run out of ways to change the subject. Tomás is going to ask everybody.

chapters.title: Nadie sabe nada
chapters.hook: Hernando has left early for the first time in forty years, and a photo says 1978. Tomorrow Hernando comes back, and he has a story about the café.

chapters.title: La máquina de discos
chapters.hook: Tomás has promised to fix the counter tomorrow, and Hernando says Rosa never once fixed it. Tomorrow Tomás finds out why.

chapters.title: Enero, febrero, marzo
chapters.hook: An old envelope has fallen out of Rosa's notebook. It was never posted, and it has a man's name on it.

chapters.title: Una carta sin estampilla
chapters.hook: Vale has read one line of a letter that waited forty-seven years, and she cannot say it out loud. Now it is in Tomás's hand.

chapters.title: Joaquín, mi hermano
chapters.hook: Tomás has a room, a balcony with a view of the cathedral, and a shower that works one day in three. Tomorrow at five in the morning he finds out which day it is.

chapters.title: La nevera de Gloria
chapters.hook: Two men from Altamira are standing in the street below, and Tomás still hasn't had a shower. He is going down to find out what they are doing to the block.

chapters.title: Ocho metros
chapters.hook: Grupo Altamira already has the café's measurements, and Hernando has finally said Joaquín's name out loud. Soon somebody from Altamira comes in for a coffee.

chapters.title: El traje de domingo
chapters.hook: A stranger in a beautiful, expensive suit has ordered the first cappuccino in the history of La Esquina de Rosa, and Simón has gone quiet. Tomorrow the stranger wants to talk.

chapters.title: Hoteles con paisaje
chapters.hook: Ricardo Altamira himself has been in the café, drunk a cappuccino and asked Tomás to sell. That night Tomás is looking at his suitcase.

chapters.title: Día treinta
chapters.hook: Tomás has lost the bet, and he is staying in Bogotá for three hundred and sixty five days. Tomorrow at five in the morning the first one begins.

chapters.title: Agua fría
chapters.hook: Tomás has said yes to a job interview with a company in Toronto, on Thursday at eight. He has not told Vale, and he is wearing Rosa's watch.

chapters.title: La rutina de la pizarra
chapters.hook: It is Thursday night and Tomás is behind the flour room door again. Tomorrow's bread has to be made tonight, and every bag of flour in the café is in there with him.

chapters.title: Ya es tarde
chapters.hook: Vale doesn't speak English, but she understood one word: Toronto. Tomorrow at five he has a café to open and an apology to make, and Vale is not answering her phone.

chapters.title: Una carta sin precios
chapters.hook: Saturday: ajiaco for the first time, a famous food blogger somewhere in La Candelaria, and Tomás is the waiter. His Spanish has never served a table.

chapters.title: No la recomiendo
chapters.hook: The blogger left an empty plate and a big tip, and she took her notebook full of notes with her. Somewhere in Bogotá tonight, she is writing about La Esquina de Rosa.

chapters.title: La fila
chapters.hook: One bite of almojábana and Tomás is six years old again, sitting on Rosa's counter while she sings. Tonight at seven, with Vale, he starts to remember.

chapters.title: Los domingos de Rosa
chapters.hook: A woman outside has been watching Tomás through the café window, and she has written something down. Tomorrow she comes in and orders the last almojábana.

chapters.title: La niña de las gafas
chapters.hook: Mariana is investigating Altamira, which bought her parents' house, and she says the exam is tomorrow. Tomás is going to help her, and Vale has not met her yet.

chapters.title: Al otro lado
chapters.hook: Rosa paid rent on the café for forty seven years and never said who owned it, and Altamira is already looking for that person. Tonight the rain comes, and the lights go out.

chapters.title: Se fue la luz
chapters.hook: Someone is pulling bricks out of the counter where Rosa hid her notebook, and the only one greeting them is Simón. Tomorrow somebody finds a light.

chapters.title: La gorra
chapters.hook: The man in the Altamira cap ran away before he finished. Behind the loose bricks there is something he didn't manage to take.

chapters.title: La llave de Joaquín
chapters.hook: Calle 100 is far to the north, a whole city away from La Candelaria. Tomorrow Tomás sets off to find the notary, with Joaquín's key in one pocket and no idea how the buses work.

chapters.title: Dos tarjetas
chapters.hook: Tomás is at the far southern end of the city at eight in the morning, the notary closes at noon, and a coffee seller has just asked if he's lost. Tomorrow two strangers give him directions, and they don't agree at all.

chapters.title: Dos rutas
chapters.hook: Tomás has finally reached Calle 100, but the notary is on Carrera 7, still a long way off, and it is half past eleven. The old yellow taxi honking at him belongs to Hernando, and it has a name.

chapters.title: La Burra
chapters.hook: Without Rosa's original deed, the notary's office won't show the papers, and Altamira was asking for them only yesterday. Hernando is staring at Joaquín's key, and Tomás thinks the old man knows more than he says.

chapters.title: La última frase
chapters.hook: Vale is on a mountain road with no signal, and Tomás has news too big for his phone Spanish. Tonight he tries to write her the longest message of his life.

chapters.title: Un abrazo, Tomás
chapters.hook: Vale has read the message, started to type and stopped. By morning her answer arrives, and it is exactly one word long.

chapters.title: Listo
chapters.hook: Vale is back tomorrow at six, and Tomás has promised to be waiting with a coffee. But he walked home soaked to the skin, and by midnight he is shivering.

chapters.title: Treinta y nueve
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Hernando comes to visit the patient, with Simón on his shoulder. He has a lot of very strange questions about Tomás's health.

chapters.title: Del pie a la oreja
chapters.hook: Hernando has an appointment with a heart doctor on Thursday, and Tomás has promised not to tell Vale. The only other witness is Simón, who repeats everything. Tomorrow Tomás is back at the café, and Vale can read his face like a recipe.

chapters.title: Modo avión
chapters.hook: Tomás has promised to go with Hernando to the heart doctor on Thursday at eight, and told Vale he is shopping for chairs in San Victorino. Vale loves the idea. She will be waiting for him there at nine.

chapters.title: Setecientos mil
chapters.hook: Tomorrow the purple armchair arrives at the café, and Vale wants a serious talk. Tomás is sure she knows about the doctor.

chapters.title: Un color muy moderno
chapters.hook: The purple armchair is spending the night on the pavement, and tomorrow Tomás has to return it alone, in Spanish. Vale has refused to help.

chapters.title: Nuestra esquina
chapters.hook: Altamira is buying armchairs for a hotel on the café's own corner, as if the sale were already done. On Monday night Tomás tells Mariana, and Mariana wants an answer about the salsa night.

chapters.title: Tres vueltas
chapters.hook: Tomás has four days, three plans and zero turns. Tomorrow the yellow papers turn out to be tickets, and a fourth invitation arrives for the worst possible night.

chapters.title: Boleros y salsa
chapters.hook: Boleros at seven, salsa at eight, football on Sunday, and Tomás still hasn't learned a single turn. Tomorrow three online salsa classes arrive, and Friday arrives right behind them.

chapters.title: Uno, dos, tres
chapters.hook: In Medellín everybody dances, even Vale's grandmother, and Tomás knows exactly one turn. Soon there is a bus to catch, a whole family to meet, and nobody there will dance on four.

chapters.title: Ida y vuelta
chapters.hook: Vale is asleep on Tomás's shoulder, Rosa's last packet of coffee is in the hold, and nine hours of mountain road lie ahead. Not all of the luggage is going to arrive.

chapters.title: Once horas de curvas
chapters.hook: The suitcase has vanished somewhere between Bogotá and Medellín, and the party is the day after tomorrow. Tomorrow Tomás meets the bus company, and its least interested employee.

chapters.title: Asiento trece
chapters.hook: The suitcase is coming back on tomorrow's bus, with Rosa's coffee inside, if the passenger keeps his promise. And before the party, Vale's mother wants Tomás alone.

chapters.title: Una amiga mía
chapters.hook: Beatriz has kept Rosa's secret for thirty-six years, and Vale doesn't know a word of it. On Sunday's bus back to Bogotá, Tomás has nine hours of bends to decide whether to tell her.

chapters.title: ¿De parte de quién?
chapters.hook: Mariana offers to put a proper job ad online. Twenty people answer it, and one of them turns up late, carrying half a bicycle.

chapters.title: Una rueda de bicicleta
chapters.hook: Altamira knows about the new waiter, and he is suddenly very interested in the café's papers. Two days later, a man from the city walks in with an armful of them.

chapters.title: Quince días
chapters.hook: Fifteen days to save the café's permits, an inspector who never said Altamira's name, and now Simón is gone. Nobody saw him leave.

chapters.title: ¿Dónde está Simón?
chapters.hook: Hernando has until Saturday's rains to find Simón. Tomorrow he drives the Burra round the whole city, and he makes a promise he may not be able to keep.

chapters.title: Antes de los truenos
chapters.hook: A man with a big box and a black car, late on Wednesday night, the night Simón vanished. Tomorrow Gloria tells the whole story, and her cat is the first suspect.

chapters.title: Luna llena
chapters.hook: Something green is shouting in English in the lobby of Grupo Altamira. The rain is due this afternoon, and Hernando's promise has a few hours left.

chapters.title: Solo unos meses
chapters.hook: Simón is home, Vale is laughing again, and Altamira's box says more than he does. Tomorrow Tomás asks Vale a question with that word in it: partner.

chapters.title: Cincuenta y cincuenta
chapters.hook: Tomás has promised a real contract, Vale has one more condition she won't name yet, and Altamira's envelope is still sitting on the table. Tomorrow somebody opens it.

chapters.title: El peor enemigo del pez
chapters.hook: Tomás and Vale are no longer speaking to each other, only through Jhon Fredy. Tomorrow a customer walks in with a baby and an enormous order, right into the middle of it.

chapters.title: Casado con mi taxi
chapters.hook: Tonight, in Rosa's kitchen: a cake for a hundred and twenty and a contract for two. Tomás has never made a cake, and Vale still hasn't said how long he has to promise to stay.

chapters.title: Sin fecha
chapters.hook: Vale will sign on Saturday, after the wedding cake, and Saturday is her birthday. Tomás has three days, no idea, and a whole café that is suddenly very good at keeping secrets.

chapters.title: ¡Sorpresa!
chapters.hook: The party is over, the contract is signed, and Hernando's phone has rung at an hour when it never rings. On Monday the inspector is due back too.

chapters.title: El tiempo vuela
chapters.hook: Tomorrow is the funeral, and Tomás has never been to one in Spanish. He has one night to learn what you write to a friend who has lost his oldest friend.

chapters.title: Cuarenta y siete diciembres
chapters.hook: To fight the fine in front of a judge, the café needs every paper in the owners' names, and Rosa kept hers in three boxes with no order at all. Tomorrow Tomás meets Colombian paperwork.

chapters.title: ¿Cuál de las dos?
chapters.hook: The bank wants the café's latest phone bill, for a phone Rosa got rid of in 2014. Tomorrow Tomás goes looking for a bill that shouldn't exist, and finds twelve years of them.

chapters.title: Marque estrella
chapters.hook: Somebody is coming tomorrow to repair a line that has had no phone on it for twelve years. Rosa kept the number alive for Joaquín, and now Tomás needs a phone to plug into it.

chapters.title: El teléfono de oro
chapters.hook: The line was Joaquín's, the phone was Rosa's, and the first call on it in twelve years is Mariana at the deeds office. The computers there are down, but she has found something from 1978.

chapters.title: Mitad y mitad
chapters.hook: Half of Rosa's café belongs to a man who left for the coast in 1978 and never came back. Tomás is looking for him now, and he is not the only one who has worked out what that half is worth.

chapters.title: Dos años sin arriendo
chapters.hook: In the morning, Doña Gloria has a flat in Chapinero waiting for Tomás, and a postcard from Medellín has arrived for Vale. Suddenly everybody has an opinion about where they should live.

chapters.title: Estrato cuatro
chapters.hook: Tonight, after closing, Tomás and Vale sit down to weigh it all up, reason by reason. In the morning Altamira comes back for his answer.

chapters.title: La servilleta
chapters.hook: Vale's mother wants them both in Medellín for the Flower Fair, with something about Rosa she has kept to herself for years. And Hernando has already decided he is coming too.

chapters.title: Nueve horas de boleros
chapters.hook: Tomorrow they ride the cable car up to the flower farms of Santa Elena, and Tomás is offered a job no man from Toronto should accept. Beatriz's diary will have to wait one more day.

chapters.title: ¡Qué oso!
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Tomás carries a small silleta down the city's widest avenue in front of half of Medellín. And tomorrow night, Beatriz finally opens the diary.

chapters.title: El muchacho de los ojos tristes
chapters.hook: Tonight, at last, Beatriz reads from the diary. What Rosa told her in 1990 will change how everybody sees Rosa, and one person in that kitchen will hear something about herself.

chapters.title: Ni un bolero
chapters.hook: Hernando has kept something about that night in 1978 to himself for forty-eight years. Tomorrow he cooks a long dinner for everyone, and the stories about Rosa finally come out.

chapters.title: El balde de Rosa
chapters.hook: The mop water was the funny half of the story, Hernando says, and the senator came back. Tomorrow Hernando tells the rest, and then the story he has never told anyone.

chapters.title: Estimada señora
chapters.hook: Joaquín owed money, and the night before he left, something broke between him and Rosa. Tomorrow, with the plates cleared, Hernando tells them what Joaquín asked his sister to do.

chapters.title: Tinto por tinto
chapters.hook: Mariana has a story ready to publish, Tomás has a letter to write to a city he has never seen, and Rosa's café has never had so much to say. Tomorrow everyone starts writing, and not all of it is kind.

chapters.title: Cuarenta y dos correos
chapters.hook: Someone has given La Esquina de Rosa one star online, and Vale has stopped smiling. Tomorrow more reviews arrive, and Tomás starts reading them like the software tester he used to be.

chapters.title: Una estrella
chapters.hook: Altamira has stopped trying to buy the café and started trying to push them out. Tomorrow Mariana brings good news about her article, and a messenger brings a letter from a firm of lawyers.

chapters.title: Los propietarios
chapters.hook: A letter on behalf of "the owners" gives the café six months, and nobody knows who owns the other half. Tomorrow the whole block hears about Altamira's hotel, and everybody has something to say.

chapters.title: Hotel Esquina Real
chapters.hook: Altamira will present the Hotel Esquina Real himself on Thursday, and Gloria has decided that Tomás is going to speak, loudly. Tomorrow the whole neighbourhood fills the parish hall.

chapters.title: La comunidad
chapters.hook: A hundred and twenty neighbours are waiting, and Tomás has a microphone in his hand and a Spanish he has never used in public. Tomorrow he speaks.

chapters.title: Cien años de historia
chapters.hook: Altamira offers $1.500.000.000 for Tomás's half, the permits are already signed, and Vale has said nothing. Tomorrow they finally talk about the money, and they don't agree.

chapters.title: Pan quemado
chapters.hook: Gloria has heard something about a man at the mayor's office, and she has already told half the neighbourhood. Tomorrow Mariana goes to the bakery to separate the gossip from the facts.

chapters.title: El debate de La Candelaria
chapters.hook: A towel with a hotel's name on it is not proof, and Vale and Tomás still disagree. On Sunday Hernando locks the café door, and nobody leaves until they have eaten.

chapters.title: Huevos pericos
chapters.hook: Hernando heard only the last sentence, and he has walked out without finishing his chocolate. Tomorrow is a holiday, the café is quiet, and Hernando is angrier than anyone has ever seen him.

chapters.title: Binoculares
chapters.hook: Tomás has photos of Altamira shaking hands with the head of the permits office on a public holiday. Tomorrow, in the mayor's office cafeteria, Marta's nephew shows them what is in that email.

chapters.title: El peor tinto de Bogotá
chapters.hook: Vale has given Tomás his first day off in months, and told him not to show his face at the café. Tomorrow she finds out what the café is like without him.

chapters.title: Querido Joaquín
chapters.hook: Rosa wrote to Joaquín for almost fifty years and never sent a single letter, and Tomás did not want to read them alone. Tomorrow night, at the window table, he and Vale open the first envelope.

chapters.title: La chaqueta detrás de la puerta
chapters.hook: The second envelope is fatter than the others. Tomás and Vale are going to read until morning, and Hernando has a key to the front door.

chapters.title: Nuestra juventud
chapters.hook: Hernando knew about the letters all along, because Rosa once read one to him. Tomorrow he tells them about that night, and about the morning he waited outside with the Burra.

chapters.title: Cuarenta y siete sobres
chapters.hook: Mariana is bringing a lawyer at ten tomorrow, and Rosa's last letter is now the most valuable paper in the café. If Joaquín left a family, it could beat all of Altamira's money.

chapters.title: Un tinto sin azúcar
chapters.hook: Dra. Uribe has given them one clear job: find Joaquín or his heirs before Altamira does, and before the hearing in December. Tonight Vale opens a new notebook to plan the café as if it were already theirs, and she needs Tomás for the numbers.

chapters.title: Pagos en tintos
chapters.hook: Every number in Vale's plan depends on finding Joaquín, and Hernando's savings are sitting in an envelope on the table. Tonight Tomás writes a list of everything they have to do before the lease runs out.

chapters.title: El número siete
chapters.hook: Altamira's men are already measuring the café for a piano, and Mariana's question is now in twelve Santa Marta groups. Tomorrow the search for Joaquín really begins, and so do the answers.

chapters.title: Nosotros también
chapters.hook: Someone who only follows Hoteles Altamira is looking for Joaquín too. Tomorrow Vale goes to see three spaces for rent, and Tomás has to do the maths.

chapters.title: Inversiones RA
chapters.hook: A hotel guest book from 1978 has Joaquín Herrera's name in it. Tomorrow the photo arrives, and with it, his signature.

chapters.title: La J de Joaquín
chapters.hook: Someone from Bogotá has offered Ludys two million pesos for the page with Joaquín's signature. Tomorrow Tomás takes the bus to the police station with both signatures on his phone.

chapters.title: Un ladrón con modales
chapters.hook: The machine is broken until the part arrives from Italy, so tomorrow the café lives on mango pastries. Vale starts at five, tired and in a hurry, with a very sharp knife.

chapters.title: El mango once
chapters.hook: At eleven at night, just as Tomás turns off the light, something comes through Rosa's window. Tomorrow at eight they were going to the police station anyway, and now they have one more thing to report.

chapters.title: Una sola palabra
chapters.hook: The stone was a message, "Vendan", and the police now call it a threat. Hernando says the pain in his chest is just the queue, but tomorrow, back at the café, it turns out it is not.

chapters.title: Una camioneta de pan
chapters.hook: Hernando is spending the night at the clinic, and the box of pills he never opened is now in Vale's hands. Tomorrow at seven the cardiologist comes, she doesn't like repeating herself, and Tomás has to understand every word.

chapters.title: Su español es de Toronto
chapters.hook: Hernando has a prescription, a diet and orders to stop getting up at dawn, and Vale has his salt shaker in her apron. Tomorrow the whole café starts looking after him, whether he likes it or not.

chapters.title: Sin sal
chapters.hook: Sales are better than ever, but the clinic, the window, the machine part and the lawyer add up to more than the café earns. Tomorrow, over a coffee, Tomás and Vale sit down with every number, and Hernando wants to sell the Burra.

chapters.title: Montaña rusa
chapters.hook: Mariana says the café doesn't need to sell a taxi or a ring, it needs a vaca, and Hernando knows nothing about cows. Tomorrow she explains how a whole neighbourhood pays a debt that nobody can pay alone.

chapters.title: La vaca de Rosa
chapters.hook: The page is live, the ceramic pig is by the till, and the first stranger has paid back a coffee from 1987. Tomorrow begins a week in which the neighbourhood, and people nobody has ever met, start to answer.

chapters.title: Gracias, vecino
chapters.hook: The vaca has raised more than twice the debt, and the rest will pay for the search. Then a voice note arrives from Santa Marta: a cousin of a friend knows a man in Taganga whose grandfather was called Herrera.

chapters.title: El teléfono roto
chapters.hook: The man in Taganga has no phone, but every morning he listens to the radio. Tomorrow Mariana calls in a favour from the press, and Tomás has to speak live on air in Santa Marta.

chapters.title: Al aire
chapters.hook: At five tomorrow morning the message goes out to every boat off Santa Marta, with the café's number in it. Hernando has been told not to get up early, and he will be the first one there.

chapters.title: Él sabe
chapters.hook: A man called Yesid has left a Santa Marta number and a short message on a napkin. Tomorrow Tomás calls him, and the same morning Mariana's article about Altamira comes out.

chapters.title: Primera página
chapters.hook: Mariana's article has been shared eighty thousand times, and Yesid has finally decided whose side they are on. Tomorrow the whole country wakes up to the story, and the café ends up on the morning news.

chapters.title: El titular del día
chapters.hook: At nine tomorrow the mayor's office speaks about Rengifo, and at ten Grupo Altamira gives its answer. By then the café will be full of reporters, and every one of them wants to hear from Tomás.

chapters.title: Ficción
chapters.hook: The heritage committee wants a written statement in two weeks, and Tomás has never written anything that long in any language. Tomorrow Vale and Mariana become his editors, and neither of them is gentle.

chapters.title: La escritura
chapters.hook: Mariana's friend the historian once wrote about the tailors of the old town, and she has agreed to see them tomorrow. She will also tell Tomás, kindly but clearly, that his three pages are not yet a statement.

chapters.title: Una idea por párrafo
chapters.hook: Samuel Weinstein sold Rosa the house cheaply in 1979, on one condition, and the letter that says so is waiting in the archive. Tomorrow the condition becomes the heart of Tomás's statement, and he has to read the whole thing aloud to the people it is about.

chapters.title: La puerta verde
chapters.hook: The statement is with the committee, and Rosa's grandson is wanted in Taganga. Tomorrow Tomás has to decide whether he can leave the café, with the hearing coming, to collect something from a man he never met.

chapters.title: Treinta y cuatro grados
chapters.hook: Joaquín has been dead since 2010, so someone else signed his name for Altamira. Tomorrow at six Yesid takes them to the beach where his grandfather lived, and he has something to tell them about a visitor from Bogotá.

chapters.title: Viento del noroeste
chapters.hook: Two years ago a man from Bogotá paid Yesid's uncle for a copy of a dead man's ID. Tomorrow the wind turns south-west, the boat goes out to Joaquín's favourite spot, and Yesid will say the man's name.

chapters.title: Tres cervezas
chapters.hook: Yesid's grandmother is back early and wants to see Rosa's grandson at seven. Tomorrow she tells them what Joaquín wished before he died, and what he asked her to do.

chapters.title: El cuaderno azul
chapters.hook: Yesid has asked the question nobody wanted to answer: what does he get out of it. Tomorrow Tomás has to answer him honestly, without promising anything he cannot keep.

chapters.title: El lenguaje de las manos
chapters.hook: Yesid is willing to go to Bogotá, but his boss gives nobody time off in high season. Tomorrow Yesid asks him, and the flight home leaves whether Yesid has an answer or not.

chapters.title: La suegra del patrón
chapters.hook: Yesid crosses the country on Monday, and the committee is waiting. First, though, a Bogotá notary has to be asked with great respect, and Tomás only knows how to ask for a coffee.

chapters.title: Cinco tintos
chapters.hook: The heir has to get off his bus and sign at a notary somewhere on the way, and it will cost him a day he does not have. Tomorrow Tomás has to ask Yesid for that, not as he would ask a notary, but as a friend.

chapters.title: Hermano
chapters.hook: Yesid is stuck in Bucaramanga, and without a judge's order there is no lab report. Tomorrow Tomás phones the court, where the clerk expects even more respect than a notary, and Simón is listening.

chapters.title: Música de espera
chapters.hook: Altamira already knows about the fingerprint, and now his polished assistant wants Tomás in their office. Tomorrow Tomás has to ask for something with a smile, while Mariana's recorder runs in his pocket.

chapters.title: Dos grabadoras
chapters.hook: Altamira has fired Duarte and plans to blame him for everything, so Duarte has nobody left to protect. Tomorrow Mariana finds him, and the court where Tomás must deliver his request has gone on strike.

chapters.title: Huelga
chapters.hook: Duarte's words stay with everyone: if Joaquín had come back just once, none of this would have happened. Tomorrow at five Yesid steps off a bus into Bogotá, and he has packed for the Caribbean.

chapters.title: La chaqueta de pana
chapters.hook: On Monday the whole café crosses Bogotá in the Burra to reach the court before nine, through the worst traffic in the city. And nobody knows whether Duarte will turn up.

chapters.title: El globo de la autopista
chapters.hook: Tonight the café throws a party for Yesid, and for once nobody talks about Altamira. Then Tomás lends Yesid his laptop, and an email from Toronto opens on the screen.

chapters.title: El letrero feo
chapters.hook: Vale has gone home without a word, and Tomás has until Friday to answer Toronto. Tomorrow they have to talk, and Vale has some things to say that she has kept to herself for a long time.

chapters.title: Las palomas del Chorro
chapters.hook: Tomorrow the lab result arrives, a day early. And Altamira's people have started asking for Yesid, the only Herrera who has never been to the café before this week.

chapters.title: Noventa y nueve coma ocho
chapters.hook: The hearing at the heritage institute is coming, and Mariana's list of evidence is ready. But on Saturday at one, Yesid has a lunch he has told nobody about.

chapters.title: Detrás del espejo
chapters.hook: The hearing on Thursday will be public: the whole neighbourhood can come, and so can Altamira's engineer. Tomorrow a notice appears on the green door, and Mariana finds out exactly what Altamira wants to build.

chapters.title: El club de la ventana
chapters.hook: Hernando has agreed to speak at the hearing, and Yesid has written a message he cannot bring himself to send. Tomorrow night Mariana turns the café into a hearing room, and Vale plays Altamira's lawyer.

chapters.title: La doctora Ospina
chapters.hook: Thursday is the hearing, and it is also Rosa's birthday. Tomorrow at nine the whole neighbourhood fills the heritage institute, and everyone has to say what they rehearsed, in front of Altamira's lawyer.

chapters.title: La cartera de Gloria
chapters.hook: The committee announces its decision at ten tomorrow. And Altamira's lawyer looked at Yesid as if he knew him, and Vale saw it.

chapters.title: Nueve velas
chapters.hook: The committee has given them three months, and Mariana's source says Rengifo has fled the country with Altamira's money. Tomorrow Mariana starts checking every word of that story, and Yesid is very quiet.

chapters.title: Salidas internacionales
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Mariana takes her story to the newspaper's headquarters, and her editor will not publish an accusation with only one source. She has one day to find a second.

chapters.title: Dos fuentes
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Mariana's story is on the front page, written with great care. The internet will not be so careful.

chapters.title: Habría
chapters.hook: The Fiscalía has opened an investigation, and Yesid is hiding his phone. Tomorrow Hernando discovers social media, and Altamira's press office sends out a short statement that changes the timetable.

chapters.title: Cinco veces más
chapters.hook: From six tomorrow morning the machines next door start digging, and Tomás finds Altamira's statement in English for investors. The English version says a lot more than the Spanish one.

chapters.title: La versión en inglés
chapters.hook: Wilson says Vale's cousin was in Altamira's site office yesterday, in his grandfather's corduroy jacket. Tomorrow Vale wants to hear it from Yesid himself.

chapters.title: El tanque
chapters.hook: Tomorrow at eight Dr Uribe wants every word Yesid said, and Tomás was not even at that lunch. And Tomás remembers a phone call he overheard the night before the hearing, one he would rather forget.

chapters.title: El acta
chapters.hook: Altamira says Yesid went looking for them, not the other way round. Tomorrow Tomás has to choose between two versions of the same lunch, and Yesid has to explain who he was really talking to that night.

chapters.title: La placa
chapters.hook: Tomorrow at nine Yesid gives his statement at the Fiscalía, and the clerk will write down every word. His uncle has called three times, and Yesid has not said what he is going to do about him.

chapters.title: El declarante
chapters.hook: The car was Altamira's all along, and Yesid told the truth even about his own uncle. Tomorrow Tomás has to tell Yesid that he doubted him, and Altamira's English report for investors has a new paragraph.

chapters.title: Declined
chapters.hook: Mariana wants to tell the whole story with real voices, and the first one she wants on the microphone is a parrot. Tomorrow the café becomes a recording studio, and everyone has to say exactly what they mean.

chapters.title: La luz roja
chapters.hook: Simón spoke in Rosa's own voice, and the recorder was switched off. Tomorrow the whole café tries to get a parrot to say it again, and Mariana has a bigger plan for that voice.

chapters.title: El narrador
chapters.hook: Wilson works on Altamira's building site, and he wants to talk, as long as nobody can tell it is him. Tomorrow Mariana has to record a secret in a café where the parrot repeats everything.

chapters.title: Un metro y veinte
chapters.hook: Altamira's lawyer, the one with the pink tie, is coming to the café at ten tomorrow to record the company's side. Mariana has to let him speak, and everyone else has to keep quiet.

chapters.title: La versión de Altamira
chapters.hook: The episode went out one minute before midnight, with Altamira's side uncut and Tomás's line in the right place. Tomorrow they find out whether anyone outside La Candelaria is listening.

chapters.title: Número uno
chapters.hook: The episode is number one, but the steel next door has opened a crack in the big beam above the counter. Tomorrow an architect comes to measure the house, and she measures everything, including Hernando's patience.

chapters.title: Sesenta centímetros
chapters.hook: Altamira has already told the Institute that the house was in ruins before the works began. Tomorrow Clemencia brings a sensor and a laptop, and Tomás, who tested software for a living, reads Altamira's report very closely.

chapters.title: Copiar y pegar
chapters.hook: Altamira's report was copied from another house, and the machines shake the café four times harder than they should. Tomorrow at six Clemencia presents her findings to the whole neighbourhood, and someone has invited Altamira's engineer.

chapters.title: Como pueden ver
chapters.hook: The engineer who signed the reports for six demolished houses is sitting in the reserved chair. Tomorrow Clemencia climbs up to the beam for her last measurements, and Hernando, who promised not to touch anything, cannot keep his hands to himself.

chapters.title: Le falta sal
chapters.hook: The machines went quiet for exactly as long as Clemencia was on the ladder. Tonight she writes her report, and tomorrow at nine she reads every word of it in the café, including a sentence about what caused the crack.

chapters.title: Sin haber entrado
chapters.hook: The report is signed, and it is exactly the evidence they needed. Now the neighbours have to write a formal complaint to the mayor's office, with no jokes, no parce and no parrots, and Hernando is already sharpening his pencil.

chapters.title: Cordialmente
chapters.hook: The complaint will take fifteen working days, and the beam may not have them. Tomorrow the café tackles a forty page application to the Institute, full of clauses, references and fees, and every owner of the house has to sign it.

chapters.title: Cláusula siete
chapters.hook: Every owner has to sign, and half the house belongs to Joaquín's family, including an uncle who wants Altamira's money. Tomorrow Tomás writes a formal letter to doña Eulalia proposing that the two families own the house together, and he has to do it without sounding like a bank.

chapters.title: Como se lo diría a Rosa
chapters.hook: Eulalia will sign on Monday, but her son, the uncle who once sold Joaquín's identity card, is on his way to Bogotá. Tomorrow he walks into the café, and everything depends on what he came to do.

chapters.title: Las otras cartas
chapters.hook: The uncle is in, on one condition: the house has to earn its keep. Tomorrow Mariana brings in an economist who never leaves her flat, and the business plan turns Vale's pastries into something the whole country might want.

chapters.title: Hecho a mano
chapters.hook: An investor in Medellín has seen the catalogue, and he is not interested in the house or the shared company: he wants Vale. Next week she has to decide, and so far she has told no one.

chapters.title: Me interesa usted
chapters.hook: Correa expects Vale in Medellín on Monday, and Lucía is coming to the café on Sunday. Tomorrow everybody has advice for Vale, Tomás has a terrible toothache, and someone arrives earlier than expected.

chapters.title: La muela del juicio
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Lucía climbs the eighty four steps to her father's flat, and Tomás goes with them as a witness. Neither Hernando nor his daughter is willing to give in.

chapters.title: Ochenta y cuatro escalones
chapters.hook: Lucía has slammed Hernando's door, and Hernando sends Tomás back to the café, where Vale is waiting. Tonight Tomás can finally talk, and that is exactly the problem.

chapters.title: Dos tintos
chapters.hook: Vale's bus leaves at half past five, and she has said that if Tomás does not come to the station, that is her answer. Hernando cannot sleep either, and he still has a taxi.

chapters.title: Doce pandebonos
chapters.hook: Vale has gone to Medellín to see the bakery, just to look, she says. Tomorrow the café opens without her for the first time in seven years, and it has never felt so big.

chapters.title: Vale, vale
chapters.hook: Lucía wants a tour of Bogotá tomorrow and wants to talk to the pastry chef, even by phone. Hernando has a taxi, and Tomás has a pastry chef who is not answering.

chapters.title: Guía de cultura
chapters.hook: Vale has been offered a trial month in Medellín, and she told Lucía before she told Tomás. She answers on Thursday, and Tomás has to decide whether to call her first.

chapters.title: Ha sido esta mañana
chapters.hook: Vale arrives in Bogotá at seven tomorrow with something to tell everyone in person. Lucía and her friends will be at table three, and they have been waiting all week to meet her.

chapters.title: El café que habla colombiano
chapters.hook: Vale leaves on Sunday, and she still has a room to empty. Under Lucía's article a new account with no photo has left a warning, and the Spaniards are leaving too.

chapters.title: La cómoda se queda
chapters.hook: Vale is gone for a month, and the café has never felt so big. Hernando has brought fifty years of Bogotá in a box of old notebooks, and he wants Tomás to help him turn them into a book.

chapters.title: Con pelos y señales
chapters.hook: In 1978, between two fares, Hernando wrote that he still had not told someone at the café's address. Tomorrow Tomás asks him about it, and Gloria has already shown the book to somebody she should not have.

chapters.title: Hoy tampoco
chapters.hook: Hernando has agreed to three chapters, but the third one still has no name. Tomorrow he tells the story of the sheep as if it were happening now, and Vale calls with news about her own name.

chapters.title: La oveja de Usme
chapters.hook: The third chapter has a name now: Rosa dances. Tomorrow Hernando tells the one night Rosa danced in front of a full theatre, and he was sitting in the front row.

chapters.title: Rosa baila
chapters.hook: Joaquín left the day after Rosa danced, and that Sunday was the day Hernando meant to tell her. Tomorrow he tells Tomás why he never did, and Tomás proposes a chapter about what would have happened if he had.

chapters.title: En condicional
chapters.hook: The whole neighbourhood is repeating three rumours, and nobody knows who started them. Tomorrow Tomás has to find out who is saying he is going back to Toronto, before the regulars start to believe it.

chapters.title: La impresora
chapters.hook: The rumour has reached Vale in Medellín, through her aunt, and she wants an answer. Tomorrow Tomás has to tell her the truth and answer the neighbourhood, without repeating a single rumour.

chapters.title: La marimba
chapters.hook: The anonymous number rang on the other side of the kitchen wall, then went dead. Tomorrow a golden envelope from the hotel arrives addressed to Rosa, with a picture of the café's own patio inside.

chapters.title: Por lo visto
chapters.hook: The man sowing rumours from the hotel terrace used to speak for Rengifo. Tomorrow the anonymous number claims Altamira has a judge in its pocket, and this time there is a witness.

chapters.title: La torta del juez
chapters.hook: According to Osorio's source, Rengifo flies out of Miami at eleven tomorrow. Tomorrow the whole café watches the clock, and the rumour on the board still needs an answer.

chapters.title: Una margarita
chapters.hook: The hotel next door opens on Saturday anyway, with a terrace looking straight down into the patio, and Rosa is invited. Hernando has decided to go as her plus one.

chapters.title: Rosa y acompañante
chapters.hook: Tomorrow at six Hernando writes the first joke of the day on the chalkboard, facing the hotel terrace. Nobody knows yet who up there will read it.

chapters.title: Cuarenta mil
chapters.hook: Ricardo Altamira is coming down to the café in person tomorrow, to 'talk'. Hernando has left the chalkboard blank, because some things have to be said to a man's face.

chapters.title: Un frío de adentro
chapters.hook: A huge blank screen now points down at the patio from the hotel terrace. Altamira could not buy Hernando's jokes, so tomorrow someone else's jokes start shining down on the café.

chapters.title: Mamar gallo
chapters.hook: Camila's joke went up on the hotel's own screen, against her own hotel. Tomorrow someone will have to explain it to Altamira, and Camila may be paying for it.

chapters.title: La caja de lata
chapters.hook: The heritage institute announces its decision on Monday at ten, in a public hearing. Until then Hernando has called off the jokes, and the whole house waits to find out whether it will still be standing to see the view.

chapters.title: Sin otro particular
chapters.hook: Yesid is moving to Bogotá for six months to build a cooperative where nobody owns more than anybody else. Tomorrow he arrives with his father's old statutes from Taganga, and with one condition: there has to be a swimming pool.

chapters.title: Bajado en alta mar
chapters.hook: Tomás has a list of twenty names and a law that wants everything in writing. Tomorrow Jhon Fredy jumps into a pool for the first time, Tomás writes his most formal invitation yet, and someone on the list turns out to have talked already.

chapters.title: El suscrito
chapters.hook: Fifteen days from now the founding meeting needs twenty signatures, and one of the twenty names has already spoken to Altamira's lawyer. Tomorrow the neighbours vote, and nobody knows whose chair will stay empty.

chapters.title: Un asociado, un voto
chapters.hook: The cooperative exists, with twenty members and one vote each. Tomorrow Altamira's lawyer comes to talk about the wall, and he thinks a protected house will have to pay for it.

chapters.title: Cuatro tornillos
chapters.hook: The newspaper wants essays on 'La ciudad y la memoria', and Mariana says Tomás has to write one. Tomorrow he has to find out whether a man who writes like a bank can write about his grandmother's city.

chapters.title: La carta cuarenta y ocho
chapters.hook: The letters were written to Joaquín, and Joaquín left a widow in Taganga. Tomorrow Tomás has to read his first paragraph to Doña Eulalia and ask whether her husband's letters may appear in a newspaper.

chapters.title: ¿De quién es una calle?
chapters.hook: Camila is competing too, and Tomás's essay is nine hundred words too long, with a week to go. Tomorrow everyone he loves wants their paragraph saved, and only one person can tell him what has to go.

chapters.title: El embajador se va
chapters.hook: The essay went in at two minutes to midnight with three words to spare. Tomorrow the newspaper writes back, and whatever it says, Tomás will have to say it out loud.

chapters.title: Matemático y cura
chapters.hook: On Saturday Tomás reads his essay in public, right after Camila, and then the jury may ask him anything it likes. Hernando, who ran out of breath on the stairs today, has promised to sit in the front row and behave, which nobody believes.

chapters.title: Segundo premio
chapters.hook: Hernando is writing the last chapter of his memoir tonight, and next week it goes to print. He says he already knows how it ends.

chapters.title: La pizarra en blanco
chapters.hook: Hernando's last chapter is in an envelope in Tomás's pocket, and he has promised to read it for the first time in front of everyone. Tomorrow Vale arrives from Medellín, and Hernando's last notebook has something to say about the chess games Tomás lost.

chapters.title: Juega como un banco
chapters.hook: Don Efraín promised only a few taxi drivers, and taxi radios have been passing the café all night. Tomorrow at ten the funeral leaves from the café, and Tomás will open the envelope in front of the whole neighbourhood.

chapters.title: Unos cuantos
chapters.hook: At the end of Hernando's last notebook there was one more line: the second part is Tomás's to write. Tomorrow the publisher sends the back cover for approval, and one sentence on it makes Tomás furious.

chapters.title: Está bueno, mijo
chapters.hook: Correa has called Vale four times, and she has not answered once. Tomorrow they empty Hernando's flat, eighty four steps up, and Vale has to give Correa an answer.

chapters.title: Segunda parte
chapters.hook: Vale is staying, and Tomás has started a notebook called Second Part. On Monday at seven six builders arrive with a new beam, and the first thing they have to move is Hernando's chair.

chapters.title: Diamante en bruto
chapters.hook: Tomorrow the old carpet comes up and the original tiles get cleaned, and Vale wants to turn Rosa's recipes into a menu shaped like a map of Colombia.

chapters.title: El camino de las baldosas
chapters.hook: Rosa hid the jukebox key with a label saying not to give it to Hernando. Tomorrow a repairman who keeps his own hours comes to bring it back to life, and somebody will finally hear which song Hernando used to play.

chapters.title: La B7
chapters.hook: The bench goes out onto the street tomorrow. The plaque takes twelve words, Gloria has written forty, and nobody agrees on which ones Hernando would have wanted.

chapters.title: Doce palabras
chapters.hook: A man from the mayor's office says the bench is illegal and is coming back tomorrow with an official report and a fine. Simón has already told him to sit down.

chapters.title: Está donde estuvo siempre
chapters.hook: Yesid's family has invited the whole café to Carnaval in Barranquilla. Next week Tomás finds out that his careful Bogotá Spanish sounds very different on the coast, and a lady called Nelly intends to fix it.

chapters.title: Reglas para el rolo
chapters.hook: On Saturday Tomás has to dance through Barranquilla dressed as a marimonda and then sing Joaquín's bambuco in front of the whole neighbourhood. He does not sing. He measures.

chapters.title: La nariz de la marimonda
chapters.hook: Tomás sang, and Barranquilla adopted him. Tomorrow they fly to Medellín, where Vale's grandmother has plans for him at a farm a very long way from anywhere.

chapters.title: El dibujo de la bodega
chapters.hook: Tomorrow Fabiola turns eighty. The nearest shop is three hours away, she wants no bought presents, and Tomás has one night to find something worth giving.

chapters.title: Doña Prudencia
chapters.hook: Rosa's coffee cups broke during the building work, and the woman who made them lives in a village in Boyacá with no phone signal. She only sells in person, and she calls everybody sumercé.

chapters.title: El que rompiere
chapters.hook: The café reopens on Saturday with a hundred new cups from Ráquira and Rosa's thumbprint in Tomás's pocket. Leonor Arciniegas, the critic who closed two restaurants with one column, has booked a table.

chapters.title: Para chuparse los dedos
chapters.hook: Leonor's column comes out on Sunday, and she has promised to say what she didn't like. Tomás spends the night counting cups on the ceiling, one to five.

chapters.title: Un café cualquiera
chapters.hook: Tomás has until Thursday and six hundred words to answer the most feared critic in the country, in his own voice, whatever that sounds like. Meanwhile Gloria wants the cooperative to ban Leonor for ever.

chapters.title: Razón tiene la señora
chapters.hook: On Thursday the café holds its first real tertulia: a monologue, a cumbia, a trumpet, and Tomás reading his reply a metre from the critic. Leonor has said she will come, and the window chair is free.

chapters.title: El fa
chapters.hook: The newspaper prints Tomás's reply on Sunday, with something from Leonor beside it. And Vale has seen the email from Toronto, and she has not said a word.

chapters.title: Qué pena con usted
chapters.hook: Tomorrow the café opens at six, as it always has, with four cups, a parrot who answers for its owner, and a second part that has only just begun.
